title: Our Story | R&SVP – Hio Ridge, Bridgton, Maine
description: Meet Susan and Richard Voth. Our family has kept this Bridgton, Maine farm since 1941. We restored its 1820 barn with original boards and windows from the house.
heading: We kept the old boards. *And opened the barn doors.*
lede: Susan's father spent summers here helping his grandfather. Now families can gather for weddings in the barn we restored. We're Susan and Richard Voth. Susan is the fourth generation of her family to own this farm.
hero_alt: Susan and Richard Voth, smiling, at the barn door

sections.heading: Summers with Howard and Rosa
body: Susan's father and his brother spent summers here helping their grandfather, Howard Burnham. Howard and Rosa, Susan's great grandparents, bought the farm in 1941.

Susan's grandmother, Phyllis Shackley, later spent 25 retirement years on the farm. Susan's father followed with 25 years of his own. The Burnhams also had roots in town: they rebuilt the burned Bridgton Hotel as the Bridgton House in 1914.
sections.alt: A black and white portrait of Rosa and Howard Burnham

sections.heading: It started with the house windows.
body: We came back to the farm in October 2020 after Susan retired. We started work on the house. Richard wanted new windows, and Susan wanted to keep the old ones for the barn.
A friend suggested a place for overnight guests. We chose to make room for events instead. R&SVP stands for Richard and Susan Voth Properties. Hio Ridge is our road.
sections.alt: The barn in 2020: dark weathered boards, a sagging roofline, grass in front

sections.heading: The old floorboards became ceremony benches.
body: We started with a new garage because the barn had served as one for years. Tim Brown and his team at Brown Solutions restored the barn. They lowered the floor 12 inches to give more headroom above the old stalls.

We kept the original exterior boards inside and cured new boards for the outside. The house windows now light the barn. Old floorboards became ceremony benches. Greg Bouley of River's Edge Landscaping used stones from beneath the barn for the planters and seating circle.
sections.alt: The ell and barn during renovation, new boards on the ell, the old barn beside it

sections.heading: We opened the doors to our neighbors.
body: The High Street Jazz Band played as visitors explored the barn at our August 2026 open house. The Maine Lakes Chamber joined us for the ribbon cutting in September.
We want people to keep gathering here. We're on site at events, and we've pledged to donate the venue for one charitable event each year. We'd love to hear what brings your family together.
sections.alt: A stone planter filled with perennials, the field behind

credits_heading: The people who helped us restore it

closing.heading: Meet us at the barn.
closing.body: Come see the windows we saved and the benches we made from the old floorboards. Contact Susan to schedule a tour. We'd love to hear what you're planning.
